definitions.explanation: A marked section of road where pedestrians have the right of way to cross safely, typically indicated by white stripes on the pavement.

examples.english: Check both ways when crossing at the crosswalk.

examples.japanese: {横断歩道|おうだんほどう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{手前|てまえ}→手前：01001_temae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まった→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧。
examples.english: The car stopped in front of the crosswalk.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
- ⟦{横断|おうだん}→横断：01906_oudan⟧ (crossing) + ⟦{歩道|ほどう}→歩道：03723_hodou⟧ (sidewalk, footpath)

TRAFFIC RULES IN JAPAN: Drivers are legally required to stop for pedestrians waiting at crosswalks, even without traffic signals. The ⟦{道路交通法|どうろこうつうほう}→道路交通法：noentry⟧ (Road Traffic Act) mandates this, though compliance rates vary by region.
